item.title: [166] /pcg/ - Pokémon Champions General
item.description:
Altaria edition

Pokémon Champions is a free to play online battle simulator available on Switch and mobile. It features ranked, casual and private battles for both singles and doubles, and will be used for VGC tournaments in 2026.

>News
Reg MC is now live. Baltimore Regionals September 18-20th. Stream:
https://www.youtube.com/live/LhsiXLo-MIw?is=xm2Nvc2rQaxTyxq9

>Resources and useful links
Community Tournaments usage data: https://pikalytics.com/
Ladder usage data: https://pokechamdb.com/en
Damage Calculator
https://nerd-of-now.github.io/NCP-VGC-Damage-Calculator/
New Player Guide(NEW PEOPLE READ THIS):
https://rentry.org/pcg-guide (now taking suggestions and feedback)

Quick FAQ
>Do I need my own Pokémon to play?
No, the game features a recruitment system, but transferring from Home is recommended to save time and resources.
>What makes the game so much more accessible than before?
All aspects of a Pokémon are customizable with VP, a currency earned simply by playing the game. IVs are also removed.
Ask in the thread if you want any specific Pokémon, and someone will respond.
>Is there single player content?
No.
>Do I need a Nintendo Online subscription?
No.
>What's the starter pack?
US$6.99 one time purchase for 50 training tickets (fully train for free), 30 Teammate Tickets (recruit Pokemon without using VP), 50 extra box space and the LGPE trainer music. Only available on Switch for now.
>Is anything locked behind a paywall?
So far everything gameplay relevant is also purchasable with VP. Only E-Floette require ZA transfer.

>/pcg/ OP pastebin (use this if making new thread): https://pastebin.com/d2FJZdPh

item.title: [ 88] Trump, Republicans so hated that KANSAS is going blue
item.description:
https://thehill.com/homenews/campaign/6096719-hamilton-leads-marshall-kansas-senate-poll/

Democrat Adam Hamilton narrowly leads Republican Sen. Roger Marshall in a tight race for Senate in Kansas, according to new polling.

A new The Hill/Emerson College Polling survey found Hamilton ahead by 2 percentage points, with 45 percent support to Marshall’s 43 percent. Another 4 percent of respondents chose Libertarian candidate David Graham, and 8 percent were undecided.

“This poll finds Democrats with their best chance to win their first Senate seat in Kansas since 1932, in part driven by Democrat Hamilton’s appeal to independent voters, leading by 15 points,” said Spencer Kimball, executive director of Emerson College Polling.

Cook Political Report shifted its rating of the race toward Democrats last month, from “solid” to “likely” Republican, citing Hamilton’s primary win as a promising sign for Democrats hoping to break “a nearly century-long Senate losing streak” in Kansas. Decision Desk HQ (DDHQ) also considers the race likely Republican.

Hamilton, senior pastor of the Church of the Resurrection, is campaigning to become the first Democrat to win a Sunflower State Senate race since former Sen. George McGill in 1932. Marshall is vying for a second term after winning the seat by double digits in 2020.

Former Kansas Gov. Bill Graves (R) backed Hamilton this week, saying the country is “facing increasing partisan gridlock and division” and that it’s “time Kansas does something different.”

item.description:
Lunatic arrested for threatening to kill Ben Shapiro as conservative podcaster admits ‘security is a real concern’
https://nypost.com/2026/09/16/us-news/lunatic-arrested-for-threatening-to-kill-ben-shapiro/

A Kansas wacko is behind bars after allegedly threatening to kill conservative podcaster Ben Shapiro, who opened up about daily security concerns in a new interview.

Korby Allen Strube, 29, was arrested recently by Florida police for allegedly posting a spree of vile antisemitic threats on X, including a menacing countdown to Yom Kippur and insinuations something would happen to Shapiro on the Jewish holiday.

“I’m going to kill be Shapiro and hes not gonna be a-live,” read a July 31 post, with a deluge of menace pouring across Strube’s X account over the following days, police records obtained by The Post showed.

“I’ll kill you just the same. Go meet Jesus. 51 days left,” read another. “Die with Jesus … I’ll kill you just the same I guess. 52 days.”

Others claimed Shapiro would be killed “for being Jewish,” or else called him a “stupid jew,” with police determining the countdown to the supposed murder plot coincided with this year’s Yom Kippur dates.

The threats weren’t just reserved for Shapiro – Strube allegedly named President Trump, the Obamas and suggested his social media behavior had somehow led to the death of Shapiro’s fellow conservative commentator Charlie Kirk.

The posts were flagged to police by a security firm hired by Shapiro – who said the threats were “not veiled” and had a “level of gravity.”

Officials quickly tracked the X account to an address near Topeka, where Strube was found living with his parents.

Strube owned up to making the posts, police alleged, before launching a disturbed tale about government spies who were sending him messages through song lyrics and presidential addresses.

Dems now paying people to listen to their bullshit.

Texas Dem group allegedly ‘paying’ for votes, operative claims in undercover video: ‘Shady as f–k’

https://nypost.com/2026/09/16/us-news/texas-dem-group-allegedly-paying-for-votes-operative-claims-in-undercover-video-shady-as-f-k/

Texas Democrats have allegedly found a “roundabout” way to pay for votes in the critical Senate and governor’s races, according to an undercover video published Wednesday.

A Democratic operative with Texas Majority PAC admitted in the new footage released by the conservative outlet Townhall that the group is shelling out $25 per person for attendance at Zoom classes that discuss “bad things” Republicans are doing.

“We are paying people $25 to attend a one-hour Zoom class to learn why voting is important and why the Republicans are causing all of these bad things,” said Sky MacAdams, an organizing manager for Texas Majority PAC.

“So it’s like a roundabout way of paying people for their votes, essentially,” he added, calling the move a bit of a “gray” area.

Federal law prohibits payments in exchange for voting or not voting for certain candidates, with violators potentially facing up to two years in prison.

The paid relational program, as its known, compensates low-propensity voters “for their time as they reach, persuade, and mobilize their friends and family to vote,” according to the website for Relentless, a political consulting firm.

item.title: [160] ganja /out/ings
item.description:
This is a thread for enjoying a pipe while doing outdoor activities. If you ask why this belongs on /out/, you've never spent an evening by the campfire with a pipe or bowl or blunt or spliff or joint or vape or edible or dab or oil, silently enjoying the nature around you, and you're missing out.

>How to get started
Purchase a cheap glass pipe (or a simple wooden chillum) and a bag of some quality outdoor or mid-grade weed from a dispensary
or your usual guy. You will need a lighter and something to clear the bowl witha paperclip works well if you don't have a proper tool.
Pack the bowl loosely, enough for airflow but enough to stay lit. Light the corner of the bowl and inhale slow. Smoke
slower than you think you need to, the flower tastes best when it isn't cherried too hot. Tamp and corner or re-light as needed. If you still
have trouble, try different methods on YouTube until you find one that works for you. Or you can just roll it or whatever.

>smoking ganja will get you arrested
Originally, the government found that weed smokers, following a careful study of the statistics (at a time when hemp was a cash crop) were just peaceful people who wanted to grow their own medicine, enjoy jazz and engage in mild tomfoolery. Nowadays, weed is being legalized against while the average American thrashes in the thralls of poverty. Put two and two together. Marijuana is just another good thing that was under attack by the government.

>muh tobacco
Not the time or place (unless you're European.) Start your own thread.

All cannabis users welcome.
